# Latest Release (1.92.0)

[Documentation ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) ](/doc/libs/1_92_0) [Source code ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) ](https://github.com/boostorg/boost/releases/tag/boost-1.92.0) [Discuss in Slack ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) ](https://cppalliance.org/slack/) [GitHub Issues ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) ](https://github.com/boostorg/boost/issues) [RSS ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) ](/feed/downloads.rss)

![](https://s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/boost.org.v2/static/img/v3/releases-page/release-foreground.png)

## What's new in 1.92.0

[Release Report ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) ](https://s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/boost.org.media/release-reports/release-report-boost-1-92-0.pdf)

- ### Performance improvements

  `mp11` algorithms faster, container rehashing optimized, unordered large‑size rehash faster, redis buffer rotation reduced CPU.

- ### Dependencies

  Beast drops Boost.Functional, Graph drops Boost.StaticAssert, and install layout now puts DLLs in binary dir.

- ### Security & reliability

  URL fixes prevent heap overflow, uninitialized reads, and sanitizer issues; TLS certs generated dynamically for CI.

- ### Developer experience

  C++20 modules added for many libraries, `--dlldir` option for DLL install, and `find_package` now supports header‑only components.

[TABLE]

Release notes version 1.92.0

## Version 1.92.0

[Documentation](/doc/libs/1_92_0/)

## General Notes

- In previous releases, Windows `.dll` files were installed by `b2 install` into the library directory (`<PREFIX>/lib` by default), except on Cygwin, where they were installed into the binary directory (`<PREFIX>/bin` by default.)

  This has been changed to consistently install `.dll` files into the binary directory, which is the behavior most users want.

  For compatibility, a new command line option, `--dlldir`, has been added to `b2 install` so that the directory can be overridden, and if needed, pointed to `<PREFIX>/lib`.

- The CMake configuration file installed by `b2 install` has been updated to support requesting header-only libraries as `find_package` components.

  That is, something like `find_package(Boost REQUIRED COMPONENTS mp11)` works now (and defines the target `Boost::mp11`), whereas previously it did not (only compiled libraries were considered components).

  This matches the behavior of the CMake configuration files installed by building Boost with CMake, making it possible to consume Boost in the same way regardless of how it was built and installed.

  As part of this regularization, the little used feature of requesting `COMPONENTS ALL` has been removed. It’s not supported by the CMake Boost build, and was never supported by `FindBoost`.

## New Libraries

## Updated Libraries

- [Asio](/libs/asio/)

  - Added a `"scheduler"` / `"assume_continuation"` configuration parameter, which allows posted handlers to be added to a fast thread-local queue.

  - Added `"reactor"` configuration parameters for tuning the io_uring backend: `io_uring_ring_count`, `io_uring_ring_size`, `io_uring_submit_batch_size` and `io_uring_iowait`.

  - Added the ability to configure `ssl::stream<>`'s internal buffer sizes.

  - Added a forward declarations header `boost/asio/fwd.hpp` to safely forward declare Asio class names when using the versioned namespace.

  - Added an example for using `cancel_after` with coroutines.

  - Added support for `co_composed` under `BOOST_ASIO_NO_EXCEPTIONS`.

  - Added a missing optimisation for `concurrency_hint == 1` in `io_context::poll_one()`.

  - Changed all exception classes to use inline implementations, to fix an undefined symbol error on some platforms when using separate compilation.

  - Changed constants and CPOs to use external linkage for C++17 and later.

  - Changed "slim" mutexes to use futexes on Linux.

  - Changed the reactor to use `MSG_DONTWAIT`, if supported, rather than setting the socket to be non-blocking.

  - Fixed two `co_composed` crashes on MSVC, one when using multiple completion signatures, and one due to insufficient alignment.

  - Fixed the return type on one `cancel_after` overload.

  - Fixed an integer truncation issue in `basic_streambuf::commit`/`consume`.

  - Fixed a buffer invalidation error triggered when SSL streams are moved, and clarified the buffer invalidation semantics.

  - Fixed a compilation error, seen on some compilers, that occurs when using `post`, `dispatch` or `defer` with a completion handler.

  - Fixed `parallel_group` handling of non-terminal cancellation requests.

  - Fixed some thread sanitizer warnings due to atomic thread fences, and added extra thread sanitizer instrumentation.

  - Fixed a signed/unsigned warning in `basic_resolver_results`, and suppressed some case fall-through warnings.

  - Fixed `experimental::channel` compilation with older versions of MSVC.

  - Fixed the `multicast::enable_loopback` socket option size on NetBSD and OpenBSD.

  - Fixed standard library coroutine detection when using `clang-cl`.

  - Improved cross-referencing within the documentation.

  - Consult the [Revision History](/doc/libs/1_92_0/doc/html/boost_asio/history.html) for further details.

- [Assert](/libs/assert/):

  - Fix `BOOST_VERIFY` in the rare case of both `BOOST_ENABLE_ASSERT_HANDLER` and `BOOST_ENABLE_ASSERT_DEBUG_HANDLER` being defined.

- [Beast](/libs/beast/):

  - `websocket::stream` accepts close code 1014 (bad gateway).

  - `http::basic_parser` ignores connection and framing fields in trailers.

  - `http::parser` drops framing and connection-control fields carried in trailers.

  - `http::basic_parser` rejects chunked transfer-encoding in HTTP/1.0 requests.

  - `http::basic_parser` rejects `Content-Length` with `Transfer-Encoding` regardless of field order.

  - `http::basic_parser` rejects requests with a `Transfer-Encoding` that does not end in chunked.

  - `http::basic_parser` validates quoted-strings in chunk extensions.

  - `http::message::prepare_payload` rejects 1xx responses with a body.

  - `websocket::stream` rejects 64-bit frame lengths with the high bit set.

  - File operations clear the `error_code` on success.

  - The `server-flex-awaitable` example dispatches cancellation to the task’s strand.

  - Removed dependency on Boost.Functional.

- [Charconv](/libs/charconv/):

  - Added CUDA support allowing both `to_chars` and `from_chars` for integers to be used in CUDA kernels

  - Fixed support for Clang on PPC64LE as it keeps `long double` and `__float128` as distinct types which was previously considered invalid via `static_assert`

- [ContainerHash](/libs/container_hash/):

  - Hashing a valueless `std::variant` instance no longer throws.

- [Container](/libs/container/):

  - Added new `boost::container::hub` container designed by Joaquín M. López Muñoz.

    See the Hub Container chapter in the Container documentation for more information.

  - Fixed bugs/issues:

    - Wrong overload resolution protection in implementation of P2363R5 ([\#334](https://github.com/boostorg/container/issues/334)).

    - Compile error with `erase` and `small_vector<std::string>` ([\#336](https://github.com/boostorg/container/issues/336)).

    - `uses_allocator_construction.hpp`: missing `#include …​/config_end.hpp` ([\#338](https://github.com/boostorg/container/issues/338)).

  - Added `unchecked_emplace_back` and `unchecked_push_back` to `boost::container::vector`, `boost::container::static_vector`, and `boost::container::small_vector`.

  - Implemented C++23 [P1518](https://wg21.link/P1518) change: modified allocator-extended constructors for all containers so that the deduction guides for containers are not overconstrained.

- [Conversion](/libs/conversion/):

  - C++20 Module `boost.conversion` was implemented. Many thanks to [Fedor Osetrov](https://github.com/fdr400) for the PR ([PR#43](https://github.com/boostorg/conversion/pull/43))!

- [Decimal](/libs/decimal/):

  - Added initial CUDA support allowing `decimal32_t`, `decimal64_t`, and `decimal128_t` to be used in CUDA kernels

  - Added `decompose` function which returns the significand, exponent, and sign without normalization (i.e. in their current cohort)

- [DLL](/libs/dll/):

  - Fixed `smart_library` constructors from `shared_library` ([PR#114](https://github.com/boostorg/dll/pull/114)). Many thanks to [R. Savchenko](https://github.com/stima) for the PR!

  - C++20 Module `boost.dll` was implemented. Many thanks to [Fedor Osetrov](https://github.com/fdr400) for the PRs ([PR#110](https://github.com/boostorg/dll/pull/110), [PR#111](https://github.com/boostorg/dll/pull/111), [PR#112](https://github.com/boostorg/dll/pull/112))!

- [Filesystem](/libs/filesystem/):

  - Marked templated versions of `initial_path` as deprecated and removed from **v4**. Use the non-templated versions instead.

  - Use `readdir` instead of `readdir_r` on more POSIX platforms, specifically on Mac OS and other Apple operating systems, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, DragonFly BSD, NetBSD, QNX 6.0 and later, Solaris 10 and later and Illumos-based systems. Solaris users with gcc are recommended to define
    SunOS_5_x macros according to their target Solaris version (e.g. `SunOS_5_11`) when building Boost. ([\#349](https://github.com/boostorg/filesystem/issues/349))

  - Support for platforms with non-thread-safe `readdir` is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Although not required until [POSIX.1-2024](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/readdir.html), on modern systems `readdir` is thread-safe when used with separate `DIR` objects in different threads and on some systems `readdir_r` is marked as deprecated. POSIX.1-2024 has been updated accordingly and also marked `readdir_r` as obsolescent, with a planned removal in a future version of the specification.

  - On POSIX platforms, handle `EINTR` error code returned from `opendir`, `readdir` and equivalents. Although not documented, this error code, reportedly, may be returned on Apple operating systems and some BSD systems.

- [Geometry](/libs/geometry/):

  - Improvements (`geometry`):

    - Drop `varray` implementation in favor of Boost.Container `static_vector` ([PR#1458](https://github.com/boostorg/geometry/pull/1458)).

    - Refactor/reduce misc boost dependencies ([PR#1459](https://github.com/boostorg/geometry/pull/1459)).

    - Improve short-distance accuracy of Andoyer inverse ([PR#1461](https://github.com/boostorg/geometry/pull/1461)).

  - Solved issues (`geometry`):

    - Unit test `index_rtree_exceptions_rst` fails ([\#1399](https://github.com/boostorg/geometry/issues/1399)).

    - Performance regression on GCC ([\#1452](https://github.com/boostorg/geometry/issues/1452)).

    - Missing citation guidelines ([\#714](https://github.com/boostorg/geometry/issues/714)).

    - Two almost identical rectangles have no intersection ([\#1471](https://github.com/boostorg/geometry/issues/1471)).

    - Various fixes of errors and warnings.

- [Graph](/libs/graph/):

  - Added a Louvain community detection algorithm for modularity-based clustering ([PR#453](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/453)).

  - Removed the dependency on Boost.StaticAssert ([PR#450](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/450)).

  - Fixed bugs and correctness issues:

    - Corrected the types used in `adjacency_list` serialization ([PR#443](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/443)).

    - Initialized `edge_property_type` in `adjacency_list.hpp` ([PR#505](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/505)).

    - Fixed a wrong accessor return type ([PR#504](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/504)).

  - Modernized types and hygiene:

    - Added missing `const` qualifiers and replaced `typedef` with `using` in several headers ([PR#508](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/508)).

    - Removed narrowing conversions in `random.hpp`, `bandwidth.hpp`, and `king_ordering.hpp` ([PR#497](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/497), [PR#498](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/498), [PR#499](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/499)).

    - Replaced deprecated `std::random_shuffle` with `std::shuffle` ([PR#513](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/513)).

    - Silenced `-Wunused-*` warnings and removed dead test variables ([PR#510](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/510), [PR#511](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/511), [PR#512](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/512)).

    - Cleared GCC `-Wsign-compare` warnings ([PR#514](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/514)).

  - Documentation: updated the entire documentation and migrated to a new visual design ([PR#469](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/469), [PR#491](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/491), [PR#509](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/509), [PR#517](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/517), [PR#519](https://github.com/boostorg/graph/pull/519)).

- [Hash2](/libs/hash2/):

  - Added built-in support for `std::optional`

  - Added built-in support for `std::variant`, `std::monostate`

- [Heap](/libs/heap/):

  - This release is the last to support C++14. Future releases will require C++17.

- [ICL](/libs/icl/):

  - Starting with version 22, libc++ has changed some lookup algorithms of its associative containers in a way that breaks ICL’s assumptions and behavior. The library internals have been refactored to solve the problem and make ICL robust against future decisions of the C++ committee regarding non-heterogeneous lookup for associative containers ([PR#54](https://github.com/boostorg/icl/pull/54), [LWG4752](https://cplusplus.github.io/LWG/issue4572)).

  - Fixed C++20-related problems with `std::iter_value_t<element_iterator>` and GCC 10-12’s handling of rewritten relational operators ([PR#54](https://github.com/boostorg/icl/pull/54)).

  - Fixed a GCC 10-11 codegen bug ([PR#54](https://github.com/boostorg/icl/pull/54)).

- [Interprocess](/libs/interprocess/):

  - Fixed bugs:

    - AIX build fix: fix return type in `get_invalid_systemwide_thread_id` ([PR#280](https://github.com/boostorg/interprocess/pull/280)).

    - Locks in `message_queue_t` cover more code than intended ([\#281](https://github.com/boostorg/interprocess/issues/281)).

- [Iterator](/libs/iterator/):

  - Added `is_*_iterator_v` variable templates in C++14 and later, equivalent to the corresponding iterator traits.

  - The `distance` and `advance` algorithms are now constrained by requiring `is_iterator` to return `true` for the iterator arguments. ([PR#96](https://github.com/boostorg/iterator/pull/96))

- [LexicalCast](/libs/lexical_cast/):

  - C++20 Module `boost.lexical_cast` was implemented. Many thanks to [Fedor Osetrov](https://github.com/fdr400) for the PR ([PR#96](https://github.com/boostorg/lexical_cast/pull/96))!

- [Lockfree](/libs/lockfree/):

  - This release is the last to support C++14. Future releases will require C++17.

  - Added new `boost::lockfree::mpsc_weak_queue`, a multi-producer, single-consumer queue. While `push` and `pop` are individually wait-free, the queue is not linearizable and a producer that stalls between exchanging the tail and linking its node can permanently break the queue, so it is not strictly lock-free.

  - Added new `boost::lockfree::bounded_ticket_queue`, a ringbuffer-based bounded MPMC queue. The queue is linearizable and wait-free when configured with a single producer and single consumer. In multi-producer or multi-consumer configurations, a stalled thread that has claimed a slot can block progress, so the queue is not strictly lock-free.

- [Math](/libs/math/):

  - Added a degree of freedom finder to the Student’s T and Non-centeral F disributions

  - Fixed CUDA compilation where host functions were invalidly being marked as device during compilation

  - Increased testing coverage of distributions leading to several overflow fixes

- [Mp11](/libs/mp11/):

  - Improved the performance of a number of algorithms (contributed by Jonathan Poelen)

- [MQTT5](/libs/mqtt5/):

  - `mqtt_client::async_run` now completes immediately with `client::error::already_running` when the client is already running ([\#54](https://github.com/boostorg/mqtt5/issues/54)).

  - Fixed several missing length checks when decoding packets received from the broker. Malformed packets could previously cause out-of-bounds reads or excessive memory allocation. Many thanks to [Team-Atlanta](https://github.com/Team-Atlanta) for reporting these issues.

- [MSM](/libs/msm/):

  - New features (`backmp11`):

    - Provide an observer API for logging support ([\#220](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/220))

    - Forward Kleene events to actions and guards without conversion ([\#229](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/229))

    - Ensure basic exception guarantee and propagate exceptions to the caller ([\#221](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/221))

    - Provide a reflection API and serialization support for Boost.Serialization, Boost.JSON and nlohmann/json ([\#197](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/197))

    - Rework terminate and interrupt state handling and provide a `machine_state` enum ([\#244](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/244))

    - Configurable event pool and inline storage ([\#239](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/239))

    - API reference and examples are now available

  - Bug fixes (`backmp11`):

    - State machine processes events although it is not running ([\#198](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/198))

  - **Breaking changes (`backmp11`)**:

    - Events in `process_event(…​)` are not enqueued automatically anymore to reduce memory footprint, use `enqueue_event(…​)` in actions ([\#178](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/178))

    - The back-end does not forward constructor arguments to the front-end anymore, it must be default-constructible. To use custom constructors, define them in the back-end ([\#232](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/232))

    - The deprecated APIs `process_queued_events()` and `process_single_queued_event()` are removed, use `process_event_pool(…​)` instead

    - The default active state switch policy is set to "after source exit" in compliance to the UML specification. The other options are not UML-compliant and will be removed ([\#222](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/222))

    - The back-end uses its own `process_result` type with new enum values instead of aliasing the enum of the `back` namespace. The old enum values are deprecated ([\#242](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/242)) and will be removed

  - fix(back, back11): Infinite recursion with event deferral in orthogonal regions (regression from 1.78) ([\#184](https://github.com/boostorg/msm/issues/184))

- [MultiIndex](/libs/multi_index/):

  - Fancy pointer support has been extended so that `multi_index_container` iterators now store references to the elements through the allocator’s pointer type. In particular, this means that iterators can now be placed in shared memory using [Boost.Interprocess](/libs/interprocess) allocators.

  - Fixed a performance issue with hashed indices when rehashing at very large container sizes ([PR#94](https://github.com/boostorg/multi_index/pull/94)). Contributed by Daniel Král.

- [Multiprecision](/libs/multiprecision/):

  - Added `data()` member function to float128 to match the rest of the library

  - Fixed issue blocking compilation of constexpr expression templates with Clang

- [MySQL](/libs/mysql/):

  - Added a way to configure which character set the server uses by default, to make tracking more intelligent. This can be used to avoid redundant `SET NAMES` statements. See `pool_params::charset_strategy` and `connect_params::server_default_charset` ([PR#511](https://github.com/boostorg/mysql/pull/511)).

  - Reduces \`pool_params::ping_interval’s default from 1h to 10s. This improves the detection of broken connections ([PR#512](https://github.com/boostorg/mysql/pull/512)).

  - The read buffer has been optimized by reducing the frequency of data rotations when incomplete messages are received ([PR#501](https://github.com/boostorg/mysql/pull/501)). Contributed by `@vsoulgard`.

  - TLS certificates for CI testing are now generated dynamically, rather than being committed into the repository. This cleans up reports raised by vulnerability scanners ([PR#505](https://github.com/boostorg/mysql/pull/505)).

- [PFR](/libs/pfr/):

  - C++20 Module `boost.pfr` is now also tested with and without `import std`. Many thanks to [Fedor Osetrov](https://github.com/fdr400) for the PR ([PR#233](https://github.com/boostorg/pfr/pull/233))!

- [PolyCollection](/libs/poly_collection/):

  - Made *`variant_collection_value_type_impl`*`<Ts...>`'s relational operators available only when the corresponding relational operator is available for all `Ts...`, in accordance with WG21 paper [P2944R3](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2024/p2944r3.html).

  - Fixed incompatibility problem with libc++ v21 or higher ([PR#34](https://github.com/boostorg/poly_collection/pull/34)).

- [Redis](/libs/redis/):

  - Fixed a case of undefined behavior within `connection` when attempting to cancel a request that has completed, but whose handler hasn’t been called yet. This happened due to an incorrect erase-remove use with a `std::deque` ([PR#428](https://github.com/boostorg/redis/pull/428)). Contributed by `@L0rentz`.

  - Optimized buffer rotations to reduce CPU consumption when many small messages arrive in a single network packet ([PR#415](https://github.com/boostorg/redis/pull/415)).

  - Added initializers to all members in the `config` struct. This allows using designated initializers to create `config` objects ([PR#424](https://github.com/boostorg/redis/pull/424)).

  - Removed the standalone workflow from the CMake. This was an undocumented way of consuming Boost.Redis with CMake aimed to internal development ([PR#409](https://github.com/boostorg/redis/pull/409)).

- [Stacktrace](/libs/stacktrace/):

  - C++20 Modules were implemented:

    - `boost.stacktrace_dump` module for safe_dump interface

    - `boost.stacktrace_<backend>` module for each unwind/collect implementation method

    - `boost.stacktrace` module exposing best available backend implementation. Many thanks to [Fedor Osetrov](https://github.com/fdr400) for the PRs ([PR#230](https://github.com/boostorg/stacktrace/pull/230), [PR#227](https://github.com/boostorg/stacktrace/pull/227))!

  - C++20 Module `boost.stacktrace` is now also tested with and without `import std`. Many thanks to [Fedor Osetrov](https://github.com/fdr400) for the PR ([PR#231](https://github.com/boostorg/stacktrace/pull/231))!

  - Fixed `Boost::from_exception` link on MinGW. Many thanks to [Orgad Shaneh](https://github.com/orgads) for the PR ([PR#225](https://github.com/boostorg/stacktrace/pull/225))!

- [System](/libs/system/):

  - Fix `unwrap_and_invoke` for functions returning `void`.

- [TypeIndex](/libs/type_index/):

  - C++20 Module `boost.type_index` is now also tested with and without `import std`. Many thanks to [Fedor Osetrov](https://github.com/fdr400) for the PR ([PR#47](https://github.com/boostorg/type_index/pull/47))!

- [Unordered](/libs/unordered/):

  - Added interoperability with C++20 ranges to all the containers in the library: `insert_range` (plus `insert_range_(or|and)_[c]visit` for concurrent containers), `std::from_range` construction and associated CTAD deduction guides. The `boost::unordered::from_range` construction tag is provided as an alternative to C++23 `std::from_range` or when this is not available.

  - Fixed a performance issue with closed-addressing containers when rehashing at very large container sizes ([PR#348](https://github.com/boostorg/unordered/pull/348)). Contributed by Daniel Král.

- [URL](/libs/url/):

  - Fixed a heap buffer overflow in `normalize_path` for authority-less URLs whose normalized path begins with `//` ([PR#995](https://github.com/boostorg/url/pull/995)).

  - Fixed an uninitialized read in `ipv6_address_rule` when an embedded IPv4 address has no preceding `h16`, e.g. `https://[::.` ([PR#994](https://github.com/boostorg/url/pull/994)).

  - Fixed unsigned-integer-overflow sanitizer findings in case-insensitive comparisons, hashing, and `format` ([PR#994](https://github.com/boostorg/url/pull/994)).

  - Fixed decoded query-size tracking in `url_base::edit_params` ([PR#990](https://github.com/boostorg/url/pull/990)).

  - Third-round security review fixes: `url_view` copy from a null source, two incorrect `noexcept` specifiers, and decoded-length tracking when iterating segments in reverse ([PR#988](https://github.com/boostorg/url/pull/988)).

- [Wave](/libs/wave/):

  - Introduce digit separators (C++14), `module` keyword (C++20), and `size_t` literals (C++23).

  - Fixed bugs.

    - `find_include_file` incorrectly accepts directories as include files ([\#243](https://github.com/boostorg/wave/issues/243)).

    - Predefined macros (`__FILE__`, `__LINE__`, `__INCLUDE_LEVEL__`) are expanded twice when `expanding_object_like_macro` returns `true` ([\#246](https://github.com/boostorg/wave/issues/246)).

## Updated Tools

- [B2](/tools/build/):

  - Includes release of [B2 version 5.5.3](https://www.boost.org/tools/build/doc/html/#_version_5_5_3).

## Join the Boost Developer Mailing List

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)](#_)

Pick the lists you want to subscribe to. You can change these any time.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boost Developers The primary discussion list for Boost library developers. Topics cover library submission, development, review, and project-wide decisions. Posts from non-subscribers are automatically rejected, and first-time posts are moderated. Please read the discussion policy before posting: https://www.boost.org/doc/user-guide/discussion-policy.html

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boost Announcements A low-volume, announce-only list for upcoming Boost formal reviews and new software releases. A good fit if you want to stay informed without following the high-volume developer discussion.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Boost Users Discussion list for developers using the Boost C++ libraries. The right place to ask questions, share solutions, and get help integrating Boost into your projects. Please read the discussion policy before posting: https://www.boost.org/doc/user-guide/discussion-policy.html

[Start here](/doc/contributor-guide/contributors-faq.html)

Boost is publicly released three times a year in April, August, and December. Each release has updates to existing libraries, and any new libraries that have passed the rigorous acceptance process.

## Achievements

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)](#_)

Achievements capture your contributions to Boost — automatically tracked where possible, manually verified for high-value activities.

-  01
  Code Commits Commits authored to any Boost repository. With 1 contribution, you will earn the bronze badge for Code Commits.
-  01
  Documentation Doc contributions using standardised Boost tooling (Antora / BoostLook). With 1 contribution, you will earn the bronze badge for Documentation.
-  01
  Library Authoring Authored an original Boost library accepted into the collection. With 1 contribution, you will earn the bronze badge for Library Authoring.
-  01
  Library Maintenance Number of libraries actively maintained. With 1 contribution, you will earn the bronze badge for Library Maintenance.
-  01
  Library Review Formal review submissions on Boost proposals. With 1 contribution, you will earn the bronze badge for Library Review.
-  10
  Library Versioning Authored new versions / releases of Boost libraries. With 10 contributions, you will earn the bronze badge for Library Versioning.
-  01
  Mailing List Participation Participation on the Boost developers mailing list. With 1 contribution, you will earn the bronze badge for Mailing List Participation.
-  01
  News Posts Published Articles / news posts published on Boost.org. With 1 contribution, you will earn the bronze badge for News Posts Published.

[](#_)

## Badges

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)](#_)

Badges recognize your journey on Boost — from the contributions you make to the time you've invested and the milestones you've reached along the way.

-  ![](https://s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/boost.org.v2/static/img/v3/badges/achievement-based.png)
  Achievement-based Reflects the depth of your contributions. Accumulate achievements to unlock five tiers; Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum and Diamond.
-  ![](https://s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/boost.org.v2/static/img/v3/badges/tenure-based.png)
  Tenure-based Awarded in recognition of your time on the platform. The longer you've been part of the Boost community, the higher the tier you unlock.
-  ![](https://s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/boost.org.v2/static/img/v3/badges/boost_day.png)
  Boost day celebration A celebration of the day you joined Boost. Awarded annually to mark another year as part of the community.
